subject: Private deployment: keystore demarcation proposal and operator access controls
messages:
From: Jose Alvarez <jalvarez@helioshealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helioshealth.com
Date: 2026-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Keystore questions for VPC private deployment

Connor —

Thanks for taking this on. Our security team flagged a few items we need clear commitments on before we move forward with the VPC/private deployment:

- Customer-controlled keys: we need confirmation that customer KMS (Azure Key Vault/AWS KMS) can be used for model prompt encryption and that Redwood operators cannot decrypt customer data.
- Operator access / break-glass: what exact procedures would allow Redwood to access keys or plaintext in an emergency? Who approves? How is it audited?
- Subprocessors: full list for any component that might process plaintext (support, telemetry, backup vendors).
- Cross-border movement: any transfer of encrypted or pseudonymized data outside the US?

Can you send a proposed demarcation and any DPA language you recommend? I attached our internal KMS questionnaire to speed review.

Appreciate a short response and a proposed time for a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Jose Alvarez
Head of IT Security — Helios Health
[Attachment: helios-kms-questionnaire.xlsx]
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jose Alvarez <jalvarez@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Keystore questions for VPC private deployment

Jose —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a short demarcation proposal that addresses each bullet; high level summary below and next steps at the bottom.

Summary (short):
- Customer KMS supported: Redwood will integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS). All model request payloads can be encrypted at rest with customer keys; Redwood will operate on ciphertext unless the customer explicitly provisions a transient decryption path.
- Operator access: default policy = no operator access to plaintext. Emergency access (break-glass) is supported only via a documented, auditable workflow: (1) customer admin approval via the portal or signed email, (2) two Redwood approvers from SOC/Infra + on-call engineer, (3) temporary ephemeral access keys issued, recorded in audit ledger, automatically revoked after N hours.
- Subprocessors: I included our current subprocessors table and will provide the canonical list in the vendor portal.
- Data transfers: telemetry that is required for serving (latency metrics, token counts, error rates) will be masked; no user prompt contents are sent to external regions unless the customer opts in.

Attachments: redwood-keystore-demarcation-draft-v1.pdf (proposal + recommended DPA addendum).

Proposed next steps: quick 30-min call with your security team to walk the flow and then Monica (legal) will propose contract language. Marcus, could you review the emergency access flow and add technical guardrails?

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Product Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-keystore-demarcation-draft-v1.pdf]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Jose Alvarez <jalvarez@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Keystore questions for VPC private deployment

Jose / Connor —

Quick technical note on the emergency/ephemeral path so expectations are clear:

- We avoid permanent operator keys. Emergency access is realized by (A) generating a short-lived keypair inside the customer's enclave or using a customer-provided HSM to wrap an ephemeral session key; (B) Redwood performs only the operation requested (e.g., replay a single message) and returns results; (C) every action is logged with cryptographic proof (signatures) and immutable event records.
- Support engineers will only see redacted telemetry by default; full traces require the break-glass workflow above.
- We maintain a signed, append-only audit trail for all key operations; retention configurable but default 2 years.
- For backups: backups are stored encrypted with customer keys; Redwood-managed backups will never hold unwrapped plaintext.

I'll add a short diagram to the proposal showing keyflow and ticket gating.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jose Alvarez <jalvarez@helioshealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Keystore demarcation - DPA clause draft

Jose / team —

I've attached a short DPA addendum draft that tracks the technical controls Connor and Marcus described. Key legal points I pushed:

- Add explicit clause that Redwood will not have the right to use customer keys to decrypt customer data for product development or analytics.
- Break-glass limited to documented incident response where customer consents and Redwood keeps an immutable audit trail.
- Subprocessor transparency: Redwood will provide an up-to-date subprocessors list and 30 days' notice of new subprocessors for private deployment customers.
- Cross-border transfers: unless customer consents, customer data (even metadata that can be re-identified) will not be transferred outside the region; telemetry for product health is pseudonymized.

Please review and flag anything you need stronger.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_addendum_redwood.docx]
From: Jose Alvarez <jalvarez@helioshealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-23T14:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Keystore demarcation - comments

Monica / Connor —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few notes from our side after a quick review with SecOps:

1) We need a concrete escrow/escrow-verification option — our compliance team wants proof that an escrow arrangement is testable and vendor-neutral. Can Redwood propose an HSM escrow partner and an SLA for access verification?
2) Subprocessors: please provide the canonical list and identify any that will have access to unwrapped secrets (should be none).
3) Audit log retention: two years acceptable; need an exportable format to our SIEM.
4) Break-glass approvals: our preference is that only a designated Helios admin can authorize. No signed emails — must be admin action in the portal or signed SAML assertion.

I attached a redline of the DPA addendum and our questionnaire with some extra items. Happy to discuss on a call — do you have availability tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks,
Jose
[Attachment: helios-kms-questionnaire-redline.xlsx]
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jose Alvarez <jalvarez@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Keystore demarcation - next steps + call invite

Jose —

Appreciate the thorough feedback. Quick confirmation of next steps so we don't lose momentum:

1) I'll follow up with a proposed HSM escrow partner and a short verification playbook by EOD Friday.
2) Monica will integrate your redlines into the DPA addendum and return a marked-up copy for procurement review.
3) Marcus will add the SIEM-export format and a diagram of the ephemeral key flow to the proposal.

I've scheduled a 30-min call for 2026-04-25T14:00:00-07:00 and shared an invite (attached). Please accept if that works or propose an alternate time. Linking the shared draft here: https://docs.redwood.com/private-deploy/keystore-demarcation-v1 and HubSpot record HUBSPOT-12345.
